question: The direct and particularly ferocious attack and the insults against the Ecumenical Patriarchate and the Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew by the Russian Foreign Intelligence Service confirms Russia’s systematic political weaponisation of the Orthodox Church for spreading vile propaganda and challenges Orthodoxy as a supreme spiritual experience, as well as the fundamental right to freedom of religion and religious expression, as protected by the EU. In view of the above, can the Commission say: 1.
What steps will it take to immediately and publicly condemn this outrageous propaganda and the personal attacks against the Ecumenical Patriarch?
If it does take condemnatory steps, can it incorporate them into the sanctions against Russia, thus also strengthening the defence of the universality of Orthodoxy?
Does it intend to promote resolutions or similar initiatives and actions aimed at mitigating and deterring attempts by states such as Russia to break, weaken and instrumentalise Orthodoxy?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.2.2026) The Commission has taken note of recent statements by the Russian authorities concerning the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople. Russia has an established record of systematic violations of the right to freedom of religion or belief and has instrumentalised the Russian Orthodox Church to advance its geopolitical objectives.

States must refrain from interfering in the internal organisation of religious institutions: a principle firmly protected under international human rights law. Churches are meant to promote peace, non-violence, mutual understanding and reconciliation.

In this regard, the EU values the constructive role played by the Ecumenical Patriarchate, including its efforts to separate religion from nationalism, encourage interfaith dialogue and protect the environment.

The EU remains firmly committed to upholding the right to freedom of religion or belief for all and it will continue to promote this right and denounce violations of it in the multilateral human rights fora and in its bilateral relations with third countries.
